limitations: Research prototype; not a diagnosis or medical device.
Physiological activation does not identify its cause.
No astronaut validation; NASA resources do not validate this algorithm.
These wrist features cannot measure radiation dose, bone loss, immune changes or cabin air quality.
Spaceflight physiology may differ from WESAD; no spaceflight correction has been validated.
The v1 pulse detector can count secondary waveform peaks; extracted pulse rate and RMSSD need reference validation.
Summary checks cannot detect all raw-signal artifacts.
Sleep/self-report are context only; not inputs to the WESAD model.
Confidence is null: clinical certainty and probability calibration were not established.
explanation: This is a research stress indicator, not a diagnosis or proof of its cause.
RMSSD here is derived from optical pulse intervals, not ECG heartbeats.
Heart/pulse rate differs from the selected personal reference by +0.00 beats/min.
Pulse-interval RMSSD proxy differs from the selected personal reference by +0.00 ms.
Skin conductance differs from the selected personal reference by +0.00 microsiemens.
Sleep and self-report are displayed as context; they did not alter the model score.
Review signal quality and the observation trend; this prototype cannot establish medical fitness.
These wrist measurements cannot determine radiation exposure, bone loss, immune changes or cabin air quality.
Spaceflight can change physiology; this Earth-trained model has no validated spaceflight correction.
